## 🚀 Building a “Pet‑Pics & Likes” App with Supabase *(No code required – just the steps you’ll give to a developer or follow yourself if you’re a hobbyist)* --- ### 1. Create Your Supabase Project | What to do | Why it matters | |------------|----------------| | 1️⃣ **Sign up** at [supabase.com](https://supabase.com). | Every app gets its own isolated database, storage bucket, and auth rules. | | 2️⃣ Click **“New Project”**, name it (e.g., **PetSnap**), choose a password, and pick a database region. | Supabase will provision Postgres, storage, and Auth for you. | | 3️⃣ Once ready, click **Dashboard → Project Settings → API**. Copy the **API URL** and **anon/public API key**. | You’ll need these keys to connect your app (or to show a developer). | --- ### 2. Set Up Storage (Where Photos Live) | Menu | Action | Note | |------|--------|------| | **Storage** → “New bucket” | Name: `pet-photos` | Public read access so anyone can view; keep write access protected. | | In bucket settings, enable **“Public read access”** and **disable “Public write”**. | Users must sign in or be authorized to upload. | --- ### 3. Create the “Likes” Table | Menu | Action | Schema | |------|--------|--------| | **Table Editor** → “New Table” | Name: `likes` | **Columns**:
• `id` → UUID, PK, default `gen_random_uuid()`
• `user_id` → uuid (the uploader’s Supabase user ID)
• `photo_path` → text (path to the stored file)
• `created_at` → timestamptz, default `now()`
• `liked_by` → uuid array (store user IDs of people who liked) | > **Tip:** Add a unique index on (`photo_path`, `liked_by`) to prevent duplicate likes. --- ### 4. Auth Rules (Who can do what?) 1. **Anon/Public** *Read* photos → all. *Upload* → only signed‑in users. *Like* a photo → only signed‑in users. 2. **Row Level Security (RLS)** In the **`likes`** table, enable RLS. Add the following policy: ```sql CREATE POLICY "Anyone can view likes" ON likes FOR SELECT USING (TRUE); CREATE POLICY "Only owner or anyone can insert a like" ON likes FOR INSERT USING (auth.role() = 'authenticated'); ``` --- ### 5. Front‑End Flow (What the user sees) | Screen | What Happens | What you wire up with the Supabase client | |--------|--------------|-------------------------------------------| | **Login / Sign‑Up** | Use Supabase Auth (magic link or email/password). | `supabase.auth.signUp()` / `supabase.auth.signIn()` | | **Photo Gallery** | Show all photos from the `pet-photos` bucket. | `supabase.storage.from('pet-photos').list()` and display images. | | **Upload Photo** | Choose image → file picker → click “Upload”. | `supabase.storage.from('pet-photos').upload(path, file)`; on success, create a `likes` row: `supabase.from('likes').insert([{ photo_path: path, user_id: currentUser.id, liked_by: [] }])`. | | **Like Button** | Toggle like; update the likes array. | `supabase.from('likes').update({ liked_by: array_append(liked_by, currentUser.id) }).eq('photo_path', path)`. | | **Like Count** | Show number of likes (`array_length(liked_by)` or store a separate `like_count` column). | Simple SQL query or store in your UI state. | > **Tip:** For fast UI updates, optimistic‑update: change state immediately, then sync with `supabase.from()` calls. --- ### 6. Deploy (Optional) If you want a live URL: | Platform | Steps | |----------|-------| | **Netlify** | Drag‑and‑drop your folder or connect GitHub repo. Netlify auto‑installs, runs `npm install`, `npm run build`. | | **Vercel** | Similar to Netlify; click “New Project”, connect repo, set build command. | | **Supabase Edge Functions** | Write tiny serverless functions for upload/like if you need extra security. | --- ## Quick Checklist for a Non‑Developer 1. **Set up Supabase project** → get API URL & anon key. 2. **Create “pet-photos” storage bucket** with public read. 3. **Create `likes` table** with columns and unique policy. 4. **Enable Auth** – users can sign up with email magic link. 5. **Wire the UI**: - Upload page → uses storage API. - Gallery page → lists images & like buttons. - Like button → updates `liked_by` array in `likes` table. If you hand this to a developer, they’ll only need to plug in the keys and can use a framework like **Next.js**, **React**, or even a no‑code tool like **Retool** to build the front‑end. --- ### Want to Try It Out Yourself? You can prototype quickly with the Supabase Playground: 1. In the **Storage** tab, create a bucket and manually upload a JPG. 2. In the **Table Editor**, add a row in `likes` pointing to that file. 3. Use the **REST** editor to call the API and see results. Happy creating! 🎉 If you need code snippets or a starter kit, just let me know.
